Hi team,

I put together an initial crosswalk and a short evidence manifest for Horizon. Summary notes first:
- Scope: We treated the request as a limited-scope CAIQ aligned to the cloud controls that Horizon indicated as high priority (IAM, data-in-transit, backup/restore, logging, and change management).
- Out-of-scope: customer-managed keys and on-prem integrations are out-of-scope for this package; we flagged these controls in the spreadsheet with an OOS comment and recommended language the procurement team can use.
- Evidence approach: redacted config snippets, a 7-day sample of access logs, and screenshots of console settings for relevant controls. Where full SOC artifacts would be required, we provided a placeholder reference to our SOC-2 package and indicated how to request it through our security portal.

Attachments included in this message (zipped in the Drive folder linked below):
1) CAIQ_crosswalk_Horizon_2027.xlsx 
   - Column A: CAIQ control id
   - Column B: Redwood control mapping
   - Column C: Evidence filename / link
   - Column D: Control owner
   - Column E: Notes / OOS flags
2) evidence_manifest_Horizon_8742.csv (manifest with owners and short descriptions)
3) redwood-access-logs-sample.txt (7-day redacted sample)

Drive location: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink

A few clarifying points for Horizon:
- For logging/artifact review we can provide redacted logs as text files; full raw logs require a legal/POA process.
- We marked three controls as dependent on customer configuration (KMS, VPC peering controls, and some data residency items).

If you can confirm that PDF bundles are fine, we will export the spreadsheet and manifest into PDF and drop them into the Drive folder by EOD July 14.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Head of Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

Thanks Olga — this is helpful. A couple of quick follow-ups before procurement reviews the package: 

1) For any controls you marked as dependent on customer configuration (KMS/VPC peering), can you add a short recommended mitigations paragraph we can include in the SOW? Procurement is likely to require language that clarifies responsibilities.
2) For the 7-day log sample, can you confirm the timezone and whether any user identifiers were pseudonymized? We need to make sure it maps to our audit scope.
3) Can you add the DocuSign link or process to request SOC-2 if procurement asks for the full report?

If you can get PDF exports + the mitigations notes by July 14 EOD, procurement will be able to proceed with a vendor decision meeting on July 20.

Regards,
Daniel
